A milk delivery round in a local community typically starts with the driver arriving at the first farm or dairy, where they collect the milk and check the temperature. They then proceed to deliver the milk to nearby households, often stopping at different homes in the area to ensure all residents receive their share. The driver may also stop to refill the milk containers or check for any issues with the delivery. The round usually takes a few hours, depending on the distance and number of stops, and ends with the driver returning to the depot or starting the next day's delivery.
